tagline: The Eagles go 17-0 again and edge the Chiefs 24-19 in Super Bowl CLIV for a fifth straight title, Ryland Maxwell runs the career rushing record out to 29,534 yards, and Dallas falls from streak breakers to 2-15.

articles.headline: Perfect Again: Eagles Go 17-0 and Hold Off the Chiefs 24-19 in Super Bowl CLIV
articles.dek: Philadelphia won all 20 of its games, had the league's best offense and its best defense, and needed every point of a 5-point Super Bowl margin for a fifth straight title.
body: Dorren Skura's Eagles have done it again. Two seasons after going 17-0 in Y93, Philadelphia went 17-0 once more, swept three playoff games and beat the Chiefs 24-19 in Super Bowl CLIV, the 154th edition of the game. It is the club's fifth straight championship and the 13th season in which one of his clubs went unbeaten.

For most of the year nobody came close. The Eagles scored 624 points, the most in the league, and allowed 326, the fewest, for a point differential of 298. They went 8-0 at home, 9-0 on the road and 7-0 against clubs with winning records. The widest margin was 48-6 over the Jaguars in week 9. The narrowest came in week 12 in New York, 32-31 over the Giants.

The playoffs were quick work until the last game. Tampa Bay fell 40-10 in the divisional round and Detroit 30-16 in the conference final. Then came Kansas City, 15-2 and second in the power rankings. The Chiefs held Philadelphia to 24 points, matching its lowest total of the season, and lost by 5, the closest Super Bowl of the five-title run.

The usual names carried the trophy. Ryland Maxwell, "Mad Max", was Super Bowl MVP for the 6th time, the most on file, in a season in which he missed 2 games through injury and still led the league in rushing. Bones Crawford, "The Doctor", was named Most Valuable Player for the 5th time. Calvin Wingo II was Offensive Player of the Year. Maxwell's ring was his 12th; Crawford and Akiem Brock each won their 7th.

articles.headline: Mad Max Puts the Career Rushing Record Out of Sight
articles.dek: Ryland Maxwell ran for 2,141 yards and 30 touchdowns, reached 29,534 career yards and passed Sherman Brandson at the top of the Career Legacy list.
body: Ryland Maxwell took the career rushing record from Lane McCoy two seasons ago. In Y95 he made it his own. Maxwell ran for 2,141 yards, the most in the league by 386 over Maurice Vigil of the Chiefs, and scored 30 rushing touchdowns. Injury cost him 2 of Philadelphia's 20 games. He finished the season at 29,534 career yards, 5,027 clear of McCoy's 24,507.

His 396 rushing touchdowns top Skura's record board, but the league mark is another matter: McCoy scored 458, 62 more. The receiving line came back to earth after his 53-touchdown season. Maxwell caught 19 passes, and 7 of them went for scores.

Everything else kept growing. His 12th ring is the most on file, and every one came with Skura. His 6th Super Bowl MVP is also the most on file. His Career Legacy rose from 13,107 to 14,019, past Brandson's 13,540, and no player on file now rates higher. His card is worth 44,400. He is 33, and the next chase is the one he cannot run down on the field: time.

articles.headline: The Doctor Wins a 5th MVP, and Akiem Brock Blocks His Way to a 7th Ring
articles.dek: Bones Crawford threw 52 touchdown passes in 18 games. Akiem Brock made 57 blocks, 19 more than any other lineman.
body: Bones Crawford's numbers came down from his 68-touchdown season, and he won the league's top award anyway. Crawford threw for 4,271 yards and 52 touchdowns, the most in the league by 12, and ran for 6 more. Injury cost him 2 of Philadelphia's 20 games. He was named Most Valuable Player for the 5th time, level with Wayne Wilson and Ray Waller and behind only Michael Wilson's 6 and Sherman Brandson's 8.

There is a flaw in the case, and it is the same one as last year. Crawford threw 10 interceptions, the most in the league, a season after leading it with 20. Nobody seemed to mind. His overall rose from 91 to 94 and his card's value by 48.6%.

In front of him, Akiem Brock made 57 blocks in 20 games. Shaquem Goedert of the Chiefs was next with 38. Brock and Crawford both won their 7th ring, every one of them in Philadelphia, and Brock's card is now worth 27,222.

articles.headline: Wingo Takes Over in Philadelphia, and Viennes Finds New York Harder
articles.dek: Calvin Wingo II caught 114 passes for 2,267 yards and 25 touchdowns and was Offensive Player of the Year. Keenan Viennes, the winner a year ago, managed 726 yards for the 5-11-1 Jets.
body: A year ago Calvin Wingo II finished 47 yards behind Keenan Viennes and watched his teammate collect a second Offensive Player of the Year award. In Y95 Viennes was playing for the Jets, and Wingo had the field to himself. He caught 114 passes for 2,267 yards and 25 touchdowns in 20 games, up from 1,994 yards and 7 scores, and was named Offensive Player of the Year for the 2nd time. His card's value rose from 1,758 to 2,584.
Philadelphia barely noticed the change. Rookie Payton Jarrett caught 81 passes for 1,450 yards and 15 touchdowns.

New York was a harder place. Viennes played all 17 of the Jets' games and caught 82 passes for 726 yards, 8.9 a catch after 20.6 a year earlier. The Jets finished 5-11-1, and in week 13 the Eagles beat them 35-19. The ratings held up, his overall rising from 79 to 82, but the production did not. In Philadelphia he was a deep threat in the best offense in the league. In New York he has been a possession receiver on a losing club.

articles.headline: From Streak Breakers to 2-15: Dallas Falls Apart
articles.dek: The Cowboys beat the champions twice in Y94. A year later they lost every home game and finished last in the power rankings.
body: No club fell further. A year after the Cowboys ended Philadelphia's 49-game winning streak and beat the champions twice, Dallas finished 2-15, the worst record in the league. The Cowboys went 0-8 at home, allowed 617 points and finished 32nd in the power rankings with a point differential of minus 200. They had gone 9-8 in Y94.
The Eagles took both meetings this time, 32-27 in Dallas in week 3 and 40-22 in Philadelphia on the final weekend. Dallas won only at Jacksonville and, in week 15, 20-13 at the Giants.

It was not for lack of a star. Lewis Pettis intercepted 5 passes, tied for the most in the league, and his overall rose from 92 to 95. The passing game around him faded: Taco Coulter, who caught 14 touchdown passes a year ago, caught 5. The schedule was tough, with a strength of 0.564, but the Jets faced a tougher one and won 5 games. Dallas had no such excuse.

articles.headline: The Chiefs Go 15-2 and Come Within 5 Points
articles.dek: Kansas City reached its first Super Bowl since Y79 behind Roc Dunkle's 40 touchdown passes and Maurice Vigil's league-leading 34 rushing scores.
body: Kansas City was the second-best team in the league all season, and for one night it came close to being the best. The Chiefs went 9-6-2 in Y94. In Y95 they went 15-2, 8-1 at home and 7-1 on the road, and won 8 straight at one point. Their only defeats came 16-9 at Arizona in week 2 and 29-21 at home to the 6-11 Raiders in week 12, the upset of the season.

Roc Dunkle threw for 4,216 yards and 40 touchdowns, tied for second in the league, with 6 interceptions. Maurice Vigil, 34, led the league with 34 rushing touchdowns, ran for 1,755 yards and passed 20,000 career yards and 350 career rushing touchdowns along the way. Shaquem Goedert's 38 blocks were second only to Akiem Brock's.

It was the Chiefs' first Super Bowl since a 44-6 loss to the Packers in Y79, and they kept it close, losing 24-19. The problem is the opponent. Kansas City has never beaten Skura's Eagles in a recorded meeting since Y88.

articles.headline: Seventeen Meetings, Seventeen Losses: The Giants Still Cannot Beat Philadelphia
articles.dek: New York lost 32-31 and 24-15 to the Eagles in Y95. Since Y88 New York has never won a meeting, and Washington's losing run reached 8.
body: Ty Lock's Giants came closer than anyone in Y95, and it was still not enough. In week 12 in New York they lost 32-31, the narrowest of the Eagles' 17 regular-season wins. In week 16 in Philadelphia the Eagles won 24-15. The series that began when Skura arrived in Y88 still has no New York win in it.

The Giants were otherwise a good team. They went 10-6-1, up from 9-8, though a week before the trip to Philadelphia they lost 20-13 at home to the 2-15 Cowboys. Lock, 39, threw for 3,488 yards and 31 touchdowns with 4 interceptions and has 627 touchdown passes in 330 games. Both of his rings came with Skura's Jets. Since Y88 the coach who won them with him has been the one obstacle he cannot clear.
Washington fared no better. The 12-5 Commanders, fifth in the power rankings with a rookie quarterback, lost 40-20 in Philadelphia and 36-14 at home, their 8th straight defeat by the Eagles.

articles.headline: Travon Swaim, 34, Is Defensive Player of the Year at Last
articles.dek: The Lions' defensive back made 232 tackles in 20 games and helped a 9-8 club reach the conference final.
body: Travon Swaim has spent a long career in Detroit without a ring, and Y95 brought him the next best thing. At 34 he made 232 tackles, second in the league to the 238 Isaiah Pinkney made for the Ravens, intercepted 3 passes and was named Defensive Player of the Year for the first time. He played all 20 of Detroit's games, playoffs included.

The Lions went 9-8 with a point differential of minus 56, then won twice in the playoffs before the Eagles beat them 30-16 in the conference final. Philadelphia had already beaten them 54-13 in week 5. Defensive lineman Landon Irwin, 22, led the league with 5 sacks.

The award moved Swaim's whole case. His Career Legacy climbed from 6,428 to 7,551 and his card's value more than doubled, from 2,459 to 5,983. He has 2,865 career tackles and 33 interceptions in 249 games. Every Defensive Player of the Year award on league cards has gone to a defensive back, and the newest one went to a player who waited longer than most.

articles.headline: Rookies Who Did Not Wait: Herbig, Howell, Rosas and Jarrett
articles.dek: Bryant Herbig threw 30 touchdown passes for the 12-5 Commanders, Tee Rosas tied for the league lead in interceptions, and Payton Jarrett won a ring.
body: Nineteen new players reached league cards in Y95, and several of them played like veterans. Bryant Herbig, 21, threw for 3,904 yards and 30 touchdowns with 3 interceptions for Washington, which went 12-5 and finished fifth in the power rankings. His tight end, fellow rookie Ulysees Howell, caught 107 passes, the fourth most in the league, though for only 551 yards, 5.1 a catch.
On defense Tee Rosas intercepted 5 passes for the 8-9 Steelers, tied with Lewis Pettis and Akayleb Samia for the league lead, and made 208 tackles. Teair Dye, 21, made 212 tackles for the Bengals.

The best rookie season came in Philadelphia. Payton Jarrett, 21, caught 81 passes for 1,450 yards and 15 touchdowns, second only to Calvin Wingo II in receiving yards, and won a ring in his first year. His card sells for 13. On that evidence, it will not stay there for long.

articles.headline: Two Interceptions From Hobbs: Brooker and Pettis Close In Together
articles.dek: Jamon Brooker and Lewis Pettis each have 41 career interceptions, 2 short of Damar Hobbs. Siran Spector moved to second on the rushing touchdown list.
body: Damar Hobbs's career interception record of 43 has two challengers, and they are tied. Jamon Brooker of the Packers picked off 1 pass in Y95 and Lewis Pettis of the Cowboys 5, and both finished at 41. Brooker is 32 and Pettis 34, so the clock is part of the race.

Siran Spector ran for 23 touchdowns for the Texans and reached 425, past Danny Diggs's 408 and Tim Wright's 417. Only Lane McCoy, with 458, has more, and Spector is 33 away. He also passed 20,000 career rushing yards.

One chase stopped. Kyron Atwell did not play a game in Y95 and stays at 3,059 tackles, 126 short of K'Lavon Settle's record 3,185. Another finally moved: Deshone Bello of the Jets got the sack he needed and drew level with Kalif Suh at 24.

articles.headline: Quick Hits
articles.dek: Shootouts, a one-point thriller, a 39-year-old passer and three ties from around the league.
body: The Packers beat the Bears 64-53 in week 18, 117 points in all, the highest-scoring game of the season.
The Buccaneers beat the Packers 48-47 in week 7, 95 points in all and decided by 1.
Dustin Milton, 39, threw 40 touchdown passes and 2 interceptions for the 11-5-1 Patriots.
The Panthers allowed 653 points, the most in the league, and went 3-14.
The Browns scored 622 points, second only to the Eagles, and went 1-7 on the road.
Snoop Dotson made 102 tackles, the most by any linebacker, with 3 sacks and 2 forced fumbles, and won his 6th ring.
Three games ended in ties, among them the Bears and Giants at 27-27 in week 3.

didYouKnow.text: Ryland Maxwell's Career Legacy of 14,019 is now the highest on file, ahead of Sherman Brandson's 13,540.
Ryland Maxwell has 12 rings and 6 Super Bowl MVPs, both the most on file. Dorren Skura coached him to every ring, with the Jets, the Falcons and the Eagles.
Bones Crawford threw the most interceptions in the league in Y94, 20, and again in Y95, 10. He was named MVP in Y95 anyway.
The Cowboys lost all 8 of their home games in Y95, a year after ending the Eagles' 49-game winning streak.
The 15-2 Chiefs lost only to the 8-9 Cardinals and the 6-11 Raiders, two clubs with losing records.
The Giants met Dorren Skura's Eagles twice in Y95 and lost both, by 1 point and by 9. New York has never beaten his Eagles.
Rookie tight end Ulysees Howell caught 107 passes for the Commanders and averaged 5.1 yards a catch.
Landon Irwin of the Lions led the league with 5 sacks in Y95. No other player had more than 3.
Payton Jarrett's 1,450 receiving yards as a rookie were the second most in the league, behind only his teammate Calvin Wingo II.
Y95 was the 13th unbeaten season of Dorren Skura's career. His Eagles had also gone 17-0 two seasons earlier, in Y93.
